title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says it would be ‘ill-advised’ to go public in 2026
slides: Going public in 2026? Altman warns it's ill-advised.
OpenAI faces pressure from investors for liquidity.
But Altman fears public markets would force profit-first decisions.
Founders eyeing IPOs: weigh mission versus quarterly earnings.
If mission matters more, delay going public.
thread_text:
1. The 2026 Warning

Sam Altman just said taking OpenAI public next year would be ill-advised. That's a rare public red flag from a CEO under investor pressure.

2. Why Investors Push

Early backers need liquidity after years of waiting. In private markets, their money is locked up with no exit in sight.

3. The Profit Trap

Altman fears public markets force quarterly earnings over mission. Once you're public, Wall Street owns your priorities.

4. Founder's Dilemma

Every founder eyeing an IPO faces this: mission control versus shareholder demands. The two rarely align after the bell rings.

5. Delay or Compromise?

If your mission matters more than quarterly beats, delay going public. Ask yourself: would you trade ten years of purpose for one earnings call?
